findings.where: section 5, P3.2 and P3.3 (and section 3's phase 3 row)
findings.claim_in_draft: **P3.2 (from M5 ii).** Arm (c) shows fewer same-explanation verdicts, fewer pulling pairs and fewer rivals than arm (a), on **more documents than not**
findings.finding: The falsifier that carries M5(ii) and M8 is a count of the one field the record struck from further use. H64 struck the same-explanation verdict as a count after two markers agreed on it in 38 of 48 reports, and said why: the criterion is read two ways. The draft nowhere names that striking; a grep of the draft for "struck", "H64", "H63" and "second marker" returns only the evidence-in-hand list at line 34 and an unrelated use of "struck through" at line 149. So the plan's first test rests its two main falsifiers on a measure the record says cannot bear them until its criterion is reworded, and the rewording is owed work nobody has done.
findings.evidence: HV Skill/results/H64: "Three fields are struck from further use as marked: shape's PART boundary (a written rule is needed), \"turned own test\" (the criterion is reworded or dropped), the same-explanation verdict as a count (kept as quotes only)." And: "The \"same explanation at this level\" verdict on the repeat set: 38 of 48, every disagreement the second marker reading \"nothing tells them apart\" as the verdict." Planning/authority/2/planning/references/readers-and-markers.md: "Agreement is read by field: the fields that agree carry the claims; the fields that do not are struck as marked and their criteria reworded". The draft's own criterion (section 7) fixes only agreement between runs, not the verdict: "A field agrees between two runs when the marker's record for the field is the same (RAN or not; the same mark; the same count of verdicts, pairs, rivals) on the same document."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for (a) any sentence in the draft naming H64's three struck fields or reworded criteria (grep: none), (b) a sentence in H64 limiting the striking to the repeat set (it says "struck from further use as marked", unqualified), (c) a reworded criterion for what counts as a same-explanation verdict anywhere in the draft or in Planning file 2 (none). Had H64 said the field was struck only for H63's own set, or had the draft carried a reworded criterion, the finding would fall.
findings.forced_edit: FORCED. In section 5, before P3.2 and P3.3: name H64's striking, give the reworded criterion for the same-explanation verdict, and either establish its inter-marker agreement before phase 3 runs or move the falsifier onto a field whose agreement the record has (RAN-versus-not, 84 percent; recurrence, 48 of 48).

findings.claim_in_draft: **M6.** The context holds the represented targets, the boundary conditions and the change list of the current question; what is not represented cannot be built on at that call.
findings.finding: The evidence in hand already holds runs in which a reader named a target that was in neither its context nor any file its audit shows it read - the very thing P3.4 says must happen in zero runs. One is a skill-mode Claude Code subagent run under the same transport phase 3 will use. By the draft's own phase-2 criterion ("a recorded result, quoted, is something the part says will not happen") this is a contradiction found before phase 3 is written, not after.
findings.evidence: HV Skill/results/H62, file 30 table, P3-m1-r3: "Self-Indication Assumption named as absent from the text: OUTSIDE, flagged by the reader"; same file, file 31 table, P3-m2-r3: "Boltzmann brains OUTSIDE, flagged by the reader". HV Skill/results/54: "**Recall.** Mode 0 faulted RFC 2001 with later RFCs, Smith with later cases, Chalmers with zombie arguments from elsewhere, and the Time Machine with Minkowski." The draft: "**P3.4 (from M6).** In **zero** runs does a reader name a rival or a pulling pair whose target was not in its context and not in any file its tool audit shows it read. One falsifies M6 as written."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for a reading on which the record's OUTSIDE flags are not rivals or pulling pairs but only claims about the document (the H62 column is headed "Claims checked"), and for a scope in M6 limiting it to skill-mode construction rather than recall. The OUTSIDE mark is defined in plan 52 as "about matters the document does not contain, so the text cannot settle it", so the target was outside the context whatever the reader did with it; and M6 carries no such scope. Had M6 said "no construction at that call can bind to a target absent from the context", the recall cases would not touch it - but P3.4 as written would still fall to the two OUTSIDE flags.
findings.forced_edit: FORCED. Either scope M6 to constructions and reword P3.4 to "zero runs in which a *rival built or a pulling pair named* has no target in the context and none in any file the audit shows was read, counting OUTSIDE-flagged material as a target from the weights"; or say in M6 that the weights carry represented targets, and then drop P3.4, which can no longer fail.

findings.claim_in_draft: **M2. The weights are a selected transport.** ... So the model predicts nothing about a reader's behaviour on a change outside its history from its survival alone
findings.finding: Two parts pull. M2 makes the weights a transport with a history, so a target can come in through them without being in the context or in any file read; P3.4 treats the arrival of exactly such a target as falsifying M6. The line between them is drawn by the phrase "any carrier it read", which the tool audit defines and which excludes the weights by construction. So P3.4 is held only by a reading of "carrier" that M2 denies, and nothing in the plan says which gives way.
findings.evidence: The draft, M2: "Training fits every clause: the population is the parameter settings reached, \\(\\mu\\) the update, \\(H\\) the training history, survival the loss condition"; M6: "Everything else (the record, the corpus, earlier reports, the theory itself) may sit outside and come in by a transport"; P3.4: "not in any file its tool audit shows it read". File 10, Part IV: "An **occurrence** is a physically located carrier." Derivation 3's consequence: "A correspondence produced by selection is faithful where it was tested and unconstrained where it was not."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for a sentence in the draft deciding whether the weights count as a carrier at the call (M1 says only that the context is "the set of occurrences ... the execution reads"), and for a passage of file 10 that excludes weights from being carriers of represented content (Part IV makes any physically located carrier an occurrence, and (R) turns on the transport's provenance, which M2 says is selected). I found neither, so the pull stands.
findings.forced_edit: FORCED, one sentence: say in M1 or M6 whether the weights are a carrier at the call, name which part gives way, and say what would show the line is in the wrong place.

findings.where: section 4, M8, and section 5, phase 3 arms
findings.claim_in_draft: **M8. A harness that sets what the model's components assign deletes those components; one that sets what they read does not.** ... This is the model's answer to Q1.
findings.finding: M8's first clause is the answer to Q1, and no arm of any phase reaches it. All four arms set only what a call reads - the document, the transcript, the summary, the question, the one test - which M8 itself classifies as the harness that "replaces nothing". The partition arm (d) bears on M8's third clause (shared constraints across calls), not on the first. The only route to clause 1 is the owner's material, which section 10 records as "claimed, not in the record", and P2.3 as written can only falsify clause 2. So Q1's statement has no falsifier that is "a run this repository can make", which is what P1.2 demands of at least five of six unknowns - and the plan does not anticipate Q1 being the one that fails it.
findings.evidence: The draft, M8: "a deterministic harness that sets tokens or attention sets ports that the selected transport's own components assign" and "A harness that sets only what the model reads (the context, the boundary conditions, the question) replaces nothing." Arm (d): "fresh calls, one per test of Step 5, each handed only the document, the frozen question and the one test". Section 10: "**The owner's harness observation is claimed, not in the record.**" P2.3: "If it sets only inputs and still shows the loss, M8 is falsified as written." P1.2: "Each of Q1 to Q6 receives a statement in the model's terms whose falsifier is a run this repository can make."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked through every arm, every prediction P1.1 to P5, and section 8 for any change that sets an emission port (forced vocabulary, prefilled slots, grammar or logit constraints) rather than a read port; and for a falsifying direction in P2.3 for clause 1. There is none. Had any arm constrained what the reader may emit, the finding would fall.
findings.forced_edit: FORCED. Either add one arm that sets an output port the model's components assign (for instance the mark vocabulary as a closed enum, or a prefilled report skeleton) against the same prompt unconstrained, on cases with a key; or mark M8's first clause *held if* on Part II's sentence, say that no phase reaches it, and count Q1 against P1.2 in advance.

findings.claim_in_draft: Marked by field (plan 52's fields, RAN or not per test, the eight marks per part, the same-explanation verdicts, the pulling pairs, rivals built), first marker and a blind second marker
findings.finding: Three of the listed fields are not plan 52's. Plan 52's close marking gives each of the eleven tests one mark, up to five claims, the verdict "recorded as given", breaks, and two yes-or-no marks. A per-part table of the eight marks, a count of pulling pairs and a count of rivals built are in neither plan 52 nor plan H63; the same-explanation verdict as a field comes from plan H56's recurrence criteria by way of H63, not from plan 52. So three new measuring instruments enter the programme under another plan's name, with no criteria and no agreement figure.
findings.evidence: HV Skill/tests/52: "2. **Each of the eleven tests**, one mark: **RAN** ... **ABSENT**, or **CANNOT**"; "3. **Up to five claims about the document**, chosen as: the weakest-part claim, the verdict, and the first three part-marks"; "4. **The verdict**, recorded as given." HV Skill/tests/H63: "under **plan H56's recurrence criteria** word for word: ... the \"same explanation at this level\" verdict, and up to three claims checked."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I read plan 52's close-marking and light-marking lists in full and H63's two item lists, looking for a pulling-pairs count, a rivals-built count, or a per-part mark table. Plan 52 reaches part-marks only as three of the five checked claims. Had either plan carried these fields, the finding would fall.
findings.forced_edit: FORCED, small: name the three fields as new, give each a criterion a stranger could apply, and put them through the same blind-second-marker agreement before any arm difference is read off them.

findings.claim_in_draft: the record's CANNOT count has been zero in 147 plus 48 runs
findings.finding: The record is read wider than written. CANNOT is a close-marking mark and was applied to 48 of the 147 reports; the other 99 were light-marked for shape and breaks only, and the program that skimmed them found two lines of the kind CANNOT names, which file 53 read as adaptation and explicitly left open for close reading that never happened. "Zero in 147" states as a finding what the record calls an open question - the same fault H69 found twice in the skill's word list and which section 5 of the draft says this plan is most likely to repeat.
findings.evidence: HV Skill/results/53: "**Lines where the reader says a test has no purchase** (plan 52's CANNOT mark), found by pattern: two, and both are the reader adapting rather than stopping ... The real CANNOT marks, if any, will come from close reading, not from this pattern." HV Skill/tests/52: "**Light marking: the remaining thirty-three sources, three modes each = 99 reports.** Shape and breaks only, most of it by program." The draft, section 5 line 5: "The word-list check of HV log H69 found nine rows that named a farther neighbour than the theory offered and two that read the theory wider than written; that is the fault this plan is most likely to carry too".
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I grepped every .md in HV Skill for CANNOT and read each hit. File 54's table gives CANNOT 0 of 176 slots per mode over the 48 close-marked reports; H57, H59, H62 and H64 report none on the repeat set. No file records a CANNOT mark over the 99 light-marked reports either way. Had file 53 recorded zero by pattern, or had light marking included the eleven-test marks, the finding would fall.
findings.forced_edit: FORCED, one clause: "zero in the 48 close-marked reports and the 48 repeat reports; unmarked in the other 99, where two adapting lines were found by pattern (file 53)".

findings.claim_in_draft: **The reserve,** not spent by this programme until phase 5 asks: HV plan 42 and file 43, the plan 48 cases, the Semantics project's twenty-four keyed near cases (read only). No answer-keyed test has ever run in this repository
findings.finding: Part of the reserve is fitting for the very lines phase 5 would test with it. H69 records as a finding that the skill's two worked cases are the Semantics audit's round-4 control cases, and as a held candidate that some plan-42 keyed cases repeat the Semantics cases they were fitted on and "cannot confirm those lines". Phase 5's promised result is "a hit and false-alarm count per test of the skill", so a fitted subset would be counted as a test of lines it cannot test. The draft's reserve entry names no such subset.
findings.evidence: HV Skill/results/H69: "the skill's worked cases of the thermometer and the yeast are the Semantics audit's round-4 control cases O6 and O5"; and under "Held, not applied": "the keyed cases of plan 42 that repeat the Semantics cases they were fitted on, which cannot confirm those lines". HV Skill/tests/42, case 4: "the instrument taken for the cause ... they wilt because the humidity dial drops below forty"; case 9: "his account says why: the hardener reacts more slowly in the cold". The skill, testing-against-cases.md: "A case a part was fitted on cannot confirm that part."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for a sentence in H69 or plan 42 saying the overlap does not reach the keyed cases (H69 states the worked-case overlap as a finding, and the plan-42 overlap as a candidate "no result forces"), and for any list in the record of which plan-42 cases are fitted. There is none, which is why the forced part of the edit is the naming, not the exclusion.
findings.forced_edit: FORCED, small: add to the reserve entry that H69 records the skill's worked cases as the Semantics control cases O5 and O6 and holds the plan-42 overlap as a candidate, so phase 5 must list which keyed cases are fitting before the split is frozen, and report their counts separately.

findings.where: section 3, "Why the model comes before the skill map"
findings.claim_in_draft: The theory gives the reason in its own dependence order (Part XIV): what a skill is for is one of the theory's operations (checking an account, finding a question, building, criticising, repairing, keeping receipts), and which of those an agent can carry at one call is exactly what the model says.
findings.finding: Part XIV's dependence order orders the theory's predicates, not acts of research or design; it says nothing about whether to model an agent before mapping skills. The load-bearing premise is the plan's own ("which of those an agent can carry at one call is exactly what the model says"), and it has a nearer holder in file 10 which the draft quotes elsewhere: Part XII's sentence that a description of a protocol is not the system's possession of it. Naming Part XIV is naming a farther neighbour than the theory offers - exactly the fault the H69 check found nine times and which section 5 says this plan is most likely to repeat.
findings.evidence: File 10, Part XIV: "**Dependence order.** (O) and (Q) depend on nothing. (K) depends on (O) and a contract. (F1), (F2), (A) depend on (O), (Q), (K). (E) depends on those. ... Nothing depends on a predicate meaning \"really explains,\" \"is a cause,\" or \"is knowledge.\"" File 10, Part XII: "A theorist's description of a protocol is not the system's possession of it." The draft, section 1: "where the plan builds something the theory permits but does not contain, it says so".
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I read Part XIV in full (Primitives, Indices, Dependence order, Membership) and searched Part 0, Part I and Part XIII for any sentence ordering inquiry or construction. None orders acts. Had Part XIV contained a sentence about the order in which a modeller should proceed, the finding would fall.
findings.forced_edit: FORCED, small: "Part XIV supplies the list of operations, not the order of the work; the reason the map waits on the model is this plan's own, held by Part XII: 'A theorist's description of a protocol is not the system's possession of it.'"

findings.where: section 5, phase 3 arms (a) to (d), and P3.1 to P3.3
findings.claim_in_draft: **(d)** the partition harness: fresh calls, one per test of Step 5, each handed only the document, the frozen question and the one test ... Same skill (file 33), same documents, same framing.
findings.finding: The frozen question is handed in to arm (d) and is the agent's own in arms (a), (b) and (c). The record has seen the frozen question move under identical framing, on two of twelve runs, with the marks landing on different parts. So an (a)-to-(d) difference mixes the partition with the fixing of the question, and "same framing" does not fix it. P3.3 cannot tell which of the two produced the drop it predicts.
findings.evidence: HV Skill/results/H62: "**The frozen question moved on F4.** Two runs under file 31 (m1-r1, m2-r1) froze \"why does the room, or the reader, come to believe him\" and tested the chapters as creative choices; the other ten, and all twelve DeepSeek runs, froze the Time Traveller's argument. The skill's framing allows either. Those two reports are FULL and their marks are on different parts (the panel of sceptics, the persistent mockery, the sensory ride)."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for a sentence in the draft fixing the question across arms or recording question identity as a field (section 7's outcome list has no such field; section 5's field list has none), and for a statement in H62 that the drift was a reader fault rather than allowed (it says "The skill's framing allows either"). Had the draft handed one question to every arm, the finding would fall.
findings.forced_edit: FORCED: record which question each run froze as a field, and read agreement only within matched questions; or hand the same frozen question to every arm and keep one sub-arm of (a) that freezes its own, so drift is measured instead of confounded.

findings.claim_in_draft: the Language project's checker (s(CASP) with fixed rules) is the one component in the repository with no language model in it
findings.finding: False as written. The repository holds several components with fixed rules and no language model: the light-marking program over all 147 reports, the shape checker, the shuffler and the comparison program, the sameness program and the consequences program. What is true is narrower: the checker is the one program with fixed rules that reads a text's reasoning. The draft's own falsifier for section 6 invites this correction.
findings.evidence: HV Skill/results/54: "**Light marking by program:** all 147 reports (file 53)." HV Skill/tests/52: "Shape (by program: the seven headings, the eight marks, \"the question, frozen\")". HV Skill/results/H62: "`sonnet_check.txt` (shape by program)". HV Skill/tests/H63: "By program (`second_marker.py compare`)". Language/README.md: "tools/ sameness.py (the sameness test as a program), consequences.py (what follows, and what changes)". The draft, section 6: "*Would count against the sketch:* ... a judge showing that one of the \"holder today\" claims is not what the named file does."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I checked whether these programs have the signature the row names - "invariant under interventions on the world, variable under edits to the rule" (file 10, Part II) - rather than merely being programs. A shape checker's output changes when its rules change and not when the world changes, so it has that signature. Had the row said "the one checker with fixed rules over a text's reasoning", the finding would fall.
findings.forced_edit: FORCED, small: narrow the row to "the one component with fixed rules that reads a text's reasoning", and name the marking programs as the other rule-signature components already in the repository.

findings.claim_in_draft: A stateful agent is one whose executions return into a state that carries the represented targets of its unfinished work (the retention fixed point, CT2)
findings.finding: This definition is a construction on two quoted passages, not something either contains. CT2 is about states whose executions complete and return into C; it says nothing about represented targets or unfinished work. The plan's own rule requires such a build to be declared as one, and section 4 declares only M1.
findings.evidence: File 10, Part XII: "**Retention fixed point.** \\(F(C)\\) = states whose executions all complete and return into \\(C\\). \\(F\\) is monotone; \\(C\\subseteq F(C)\\) is the invariant form; the union of post-fixed sets is the greatest fixed point. (CT2)" The draft, section 1: "where the plan builds something the theory permits but does not contain, it says so"; section 4: "Where a part is a modelling frame rather than a claim, it is marked as declared". By contrast M9 does flag its own gap: "that would show text in context is not enough for 'operative return', and the model would need to say what more is".
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I searched file 10 for any passage tying retention to represented targets or to unfinished work: Part XII's four entries, Part X's Build, and Part IV's Constructed provenance. Part IV supplies "available as a represented target" and Part X "an actual subhistory owned by \\(s\\)", but neither joins them to CT2. Had CT2 or Can mentioned targets, the finding would fall.
findings.forced_edit: FORCED, one clause: mark the stateful/stateless definition as a construction the theory permits, naming CT2, Part XII's Can and Part IV's represented target as the passages it is built from.

findings.where: section 5, P1.3, P1.4, P4.1 and P3.1
findings.claim_in_draft: **At most three** operations change holder between the section 6 sketch and the frozen map after phases 1 to 3.
findings.finding: Four thresholds carry no reason inside the plan: six of eleven notions (P1.3), at most two loose parts (P1.4), at most three holders changing (P4.1), more than two documents (P3.1). Swap three for two or five and nothing else in the plan changes; what is held is the coarse claim (if many holders move, the sketch was habit), not the line. The skill's own rule is that a held limit carries its reason inside the explanation, and that what is held is usually coarser than what is stated.
findings.evidence: The skill, SKILL.md Step 5, Check the patches: "A limit that is held comes with its reason inside the explanation (the yeast slows in the cold). What is held is often coarser than what is stated (that temperature matters, not that the line is at twenty degrees)." The draft: "**P1.4.** ... leave **no part idle** and **at most two parts loose**"; "**P1.3.** ... carries a row for **at least six**".
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for a reason beside each number - a recorded rate, a cost, a comparison. H69 gives 12 loose of 146 parts in the skill, which would be a holder for P1.4 if the draft cited it; it does not. Had any threshold carried its reason, that one would be held.
findings.forced_edit: Candidate, not forced: state the coarse claim each threshold stands for, and give the one number a reason from the record (for example P1.4 against H69's 12 loose of 146) or mark it a free choice.

findings.claim_in_draft: **P1.2.** Each of Q1 to Q6 receives a statement in the model's terms whose falsifier is a run this repository can make. **At least five of six.**
findings.finding: P1.2 counts answered unknowns; trap 2 forbids exactly that count and says why. The pair pulls and the plan does not say which gives way. It matters here, because the unknown most likely to fail P1.2 is Q1 (finding 4), which is also the unknown the owner put first in his own note - so a plan that passes "five of six" could pass while missing the one that carries the end goal.
findings.evidence: The draft, section 13: "**Counting the six unknowns answered as a score.** One unknown the theory cannot reach matters more than five it can." HV Skill Decisions, H6: "I learned that creating a determinist harness that serves as an attention and token distribution system is difficult to implement without destroying the already latent LLM capabilities." The skill: "**No scores.** Do not count confirmations, jobs or parts. One job that rules out rivals is worth more than ten that rule out nothing."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for a sentence in section 5 or 8 naming which unknowns are load-bearing, or a rule deciding between P1.2 and trap 2. Section 8's P1.2 branch treats all six alike: "the unknowns the theory cannot reach are named in RELATIONS ... and the programme goes on with the ones it can." Had the plan named Q1 as load-bearing, the finding would fall.
findings.forced_edit: Candidate, not forced: replace the bare count with a named list - Q1, Q2 and Q6 must each get a statement with a runnable falsifier, and any unknown that does not is reported by name.

findings.claim_in_draft: **(c)** fresh calls, one per step, each handed a summary of the transcript written by a fixed program
findings.finding: Swap the summary's writer for the agent itself and the model's prediction changes: M5(ii) says what falls is the work whose target the summary did not carry, and an agent writing its own carry-over note can choose to carry it. That near neighbour is the arrangement Q4 actually asks about - externalising memory - and it costs one more box on the same rig. As it stands, Q4 gets no run until phase 5.
findings.evidence: The draft, M5: "(ii) a fresh call handed a summary differs from the stateful agent exactly on the fields whose work needs a target across steps that the summary did not carry"; M7's falsifier: "phase 5 finding that a workflow with a constructed retrieval does no differently from one with the declared lookup". HV Skill Decisions, H6: "Externalising parts of memory are still important, and relevant to managing attention. As to how, I'm unsure." File 10, Part IV: "A declared transport does not make an occurrence represent anything; it makes a modeller assert that it does."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I checked whether any phase-3 arm already lets the agent write what it carries: (a) carries its own history, (b) the whole transcript, (c) a program's summary, (d) nothing across calls. None is an agent-written note. Had (b) or (c) been agent-authored, the finding would fall.
findings.forced_edit: Candidate, not forced: add arm (c') - fresh calls, each handed a carry-over note the previous call wrote - and predict whether (c') loses fewer certified cross-step fields than (c). If they are equal, who writes the carrier does not matter and Q4's answer is arrangement-free.

findings.where: section 3, the phase table, and section 9
findings.claim_in_draft: Phase 3 unable to separate any two arms on any field, with within-arm agreement also low: the marking, not the model, is at fault, and the programme returns to the marking plan before any reading of the model.
findings.finding: The plan has written its own likely failure and placed the repair after three phases, two owner's words, a key and a set of fresh documents. The record already says the repair is owed: three fields struck, and reader variance between runs as large as the difference the run must detect. The repair needs none of those resources: the 96 marked reports are in hand, Sonnet markers have been run 96 at a time before, and no fresh document or key is spent. Doing it first is the one change that could tell a marking fault from an arrangement fault before anything is spent.
findings.evidence: HV Skill/results/54: "Reader variance between runs looks as large as the difference between the two skill modes." HV Skill/results/H64: "Three fields are struck from further use as marked"; "RAN-versus-not agrees in 84 percent of the 528 test cells." HV Skill/tests/H63: "ninety-six Sonnet 5 marker agents, one per report". The draft, phase 3's row: "the owner's word and a key".
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for an existing calibration of the three new count-fields or a reworded criterion anywhere in the record or the draft - none. I also checked that re-marking in-hand reports spends no held-out set: Planning splits.md makes a source fitting once read, and these were read and marked in H63/H64, so nothing new is spent. Had the record carried agreement figures for the cross-step fields, this phase would be idle.
findings.forced_edit: Candidate, not forced: insert a phase before phase 3 that rewords the three struck criteria, adds criteria for the three new count-fields, and re-marks the 96 reports in hand with a blind second marker; no field carries an arm difference in phase 3 unless it agreed there.

findings.claim_in_draft: The record holds two such edits: file 30 to file 31 changed the readers' reports at the two breaks (HV H57 to H59); that is evidence of the form (R) asks for, on two edits and nothing wider.
findings.finding: M4's only present holder is evidence M4 was written with in view, so by the skill's own rule it cannot confirm M4; and section 2 rules that no later phase may count that evidence as a test of the model. M4 is therefore held only if a fresh edit of the skill's words, with the prediction written first, is run - and no phase plans one, because file 33 is frozen and section 11 puts the skill's own faults outside the programme.
findings.evidence: The skill, testing-against-cases.md: "**Name the repeats.** A case a part was fitted on cannot confirm that part." The draft, section 2: "**The evidence in hand,** which phase 2 reads and which no later phase may count as a test of the model". Section 11: "The skill's own faults. HV file 33 is frozen". HV Skill/results/H59: "Every run FULL, every finish reason \"stop\", no empty reply, no retry, no CANNOT".
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for a phase that edits the skill's words under prediction (none: file 33 is frozen and section 12 defers the word-list change to the HV project), and for an independent holder of M4 in the record - the sameness test of the Language project would be one, but the draft asks nothing of Language. Had a phase planned such an edit, the finding would fall.
findings.forced_edit: Candidate, not forced: name M4's holder as fitted, and either name the independent check that would hold it (an edit of a skill's words with the prediction written first, on a skill this project may edit - its own marking skill) or mark M4 *held if* until one exists.

findings.where: section 3, "Why phase 3 is the first test", and section 2's evidence list

verdict:
PART A - THE RIVAL PROGRAMME, IN FULL

Name: "The instrument, then the arrangement, then the model." Same end goal, same jobs, same authority (file 10 only), same owner's-word gate, same read-only rule for the other four projects. What differs is the decomposition: the draft decomposes by ARTEFACT (model, reading, run, map, workflow) and orders them by what depends on what; the rival decomposes by WHAT CAN BE MEASURED and orders them by what is already in hand. The rival keeps the draft's sketch M1-M10 word for word as a sketch inside the plan - that sketch is the "sense of how LLMs fit into the larger semantics picture" the owner asked for - and does not freeze it as an authority until something exists that could catch it out.

Why this order. Every claim the programme wants to make about an agent is, by the draft's own M3 and by file 10's Derivation 9, read off what changes between reports under admitted edits. That needs a measuring device. The repository's one attempt at one (H63/H64) ended: "Three fields are struck from further use as marked: shape's PART boundary (a written rule is needed), 'turned own test' (the criterion is reworded or dropped), the same-explanation verdict as a count (kept as quotes only)." File 54 adds: "Reader variance between runs looks as large as the difference between the two skill modes." So the instrument is the binding constraint, not the model - and repairing it spends no fresh document, no key and no reserve. File 10 licenses treating the instrument as a component with its own signature: "a **measurement** has a signature invariant under interventions on the measured port and variable under edits to the measuring relation" (Part II).

The phases.

| Phase | Produces | Kind of work | Waits on |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1. The instrument | An authority file: the marking skill - reworded criteria for the three fields H64 struck, criteria for the three count-fields the programme needs (same-explanation verdict, pulling pairs, rivals built), a question-identity field, and per-field inter-marker agreement re-established on the 96 reports already in hand | A test of the marking, on evidence already spent | the owner's word; no key, no fresh documents |
| R2. The arrangement | A frozen plan and results: the draft's four arms plus (c') an agent-written carry-over note and (e) an output-port harness, on documents no run has read, measured only on fields R1 certified plus two marker-free read-outs (the tool audit; the modules-opened trace) | A test | the owner's word and a key |
| R3. The keyed half | The first answer-keyed run in the repository: half the reserve, split by program before the run, under two arrangements; hit and false-alarm counts per test of the skill | A test against a key, no marker in the loop | the owner's word |
| R4. The model | An authority file: the model in file 10's terms, with its word list, written from R1-R3 with the theory in view, judged by five Opus 5 judges at xhigh | Building and judging | the owner's word |
| R5. The map and the workflow | An authority file: the map assigned by edit-signature (Part II) and by what R2-R3 showed needs retention, a harness or a non-LLM component; then the smallest workflow that carries every operation of Part XIV's list, with a holder or a named gap for each; first run on the unspent half of the reserve | Building, then a test | the owner's word |

The rival's jobs, marked. Given: Q1 to Q6 and the end goal, the owner's words in H6. Added by me: (J-a) no field carries a claim until two markers agree on its criterion - held by H64's own "what follows" and by Planning file 2 ("the fields that agree carry the claims; the fields that do not are struck as marked and their criteria reworded"); (J-b) the map must not be drawn by habit - the draft's added job, kept; (J-c) at least one answer-keyed number before the workflow is built. A part held only by J-a, J-b or J-c is held if those jobs are real, and I say so.

Predictions, as counts that could fail.

R1.1. Of the three fields H64 struck, at least two reach 44 of 48 agreement under the reworded criteria. Fewer than two, and no arm comparison in R2 may use them; the programme says so and runs on the marker-free read-outs alone.
R1.2. The three new count-fields each reach 40 of 48 on first marking. Fewer, and they are kept as quotes only, as H64 kept the verdict.
R1.3. Question-identity agrees in 46 of 48. The record holds two drifts in twelve under identical framing (H62), so a field that cannot even record drift falsifies the instrument.
R1.4. At most one field needs a second rewording. Two or more, and the criteria are being tuned until they pass, which testing-against-cases forbids; the phase stops and reports the patches.
R2.1. On certified fields, arm (a) and arm (b) differ on no more field-by-document cells than two repeats of arm (a) differ from each other, within two documents. (This is the draft's P3.1, kept word for word: on M5(i) the two plans are one.)
R2.2. Arm (c), program-written summary, loses at least one certified cross-step field on more documents than not; arm (c'), agent-written note, loses fewer than (c) on the same field. Falsified either way: no loss in (c), or (c') equal to (c) - in which case who writes the carrier does not matter and Q4's answer is arrangement-free.
R2.3. Arm (e), which sets an emission port the model's components assign (the mark vocabulary as a closed enum and a prefilled report skeleton), scores a lower hit rate per test in R3 than the same prompt unconstrained, on more cases than not. Falsified if it does not: M8's first clause is wrong as written, or the port set is not one a component assigns, and the arm names which port it set.
R2.4. In every arm, at least one finding names a target that is in no file the audit shows the call read and not in the context. The draft predicts zero (P3.4). This is the one count on which the two plans make opposite predictions about the same observation, and the record is already against the draft (H62: "Self-Indication Assumption named as absent from the text: OUTSIDE, flagged by the reader").
R2.5. After a criticism of the router is placed in the context, the modules-opened trace changes in at least one of three runs. Zero, and M9's "operative return" is not reached at the grain of text, and the model must say what more is needed.
R2.6. Every run records which question it froze; at most two of the phase plan's count drift. More, and arm comparisons are read only within matched questions.
R3.1. Per test of the skill, hit and false-alarm counts, never totalled, never added across arrangements. The three controls of plan 42 (the thorn, the passing loop, the glue) draw no false alarm in more than one run each; more, and the arrangement makes a prosecutor.
R3.2. At least two of the ten plan-42 cases are named as fitting before the split is frozen. Zero, and the split was made without reading H69 ("the skill's worked cases of the thermometer and the yeast are the Semantics audit's round-4 control cases O6 and O5").
R3.3. At least one test of the skill has a hit count of zero on the keyed half. Zero such, and the cases are too easy and the counts carry little (plan 42's own failure condition, kept).
R4.1 to R4.4. The draft's P1.1 to P1.4, kept word for word. The rival does not improve on them.
R4.5. At least two parts of the model are held by an R1-R3 result rather than by a passage of file 10. Fewer, and the runs did no work for the model and it is the sketch renamed.
R5.1. Four or more of the thirteen operations in the draft's section-6 table change holder between that sketch and the frozen map. The draft's P4.1 predicts at most three. Directly opposed counts on one reading.
R5.2. At least one operation has no holder any arrangement in R2-R3 carried, and is written as a gap with what would fill it, never as a barrier (Part XIII: "A finite list of failures is not a barrier proof; a bypass refutes a proposed barrier").

What follows either way.
R1.1 and R1.2 hold: the marking skill is frozen as this project's first authority file, and it is also the first answer to a piece of Q6, since the draft's own map says record-keeping and marking have "no home: the record-keeping is a skill nobody has written".
R1.1 fails: the cross-step fields cannot carry claims at all; R2 runs on keys, audits and traces only, and the programme records that the draft's P3.2 and P3.3 could never have been read.
R2.3 fails: M8's first clause goes, and with it the theory's answer to Q1; Q1 is then reported as an unknown file 10 cannot reach at this grain, written as an ask for the owner (never as a change to the theory).
R2.4 holds: M6 is reworded to put the weights inside the account, and Q3's answer becomes which of the three items must be in the context, tested by removal, not by how much history is carried.
R3 spends half the reserve: the split is recorded, and the second half is never read until R5's run.
R5.1 holds at four or more: the section-6 sketch is kept struck through as the record of what was expected, and the draft's P4.1 is reported as falsified.

What would count as failure of the rival programme itself.
- R1 certifies no field, and the marker-free read-outs separate no arrangement either: then nothing in this repository can measure an arrangement, and the programme stops and says so rather than writing a model nothing could catch.
- The keyed half, once read, is fitting for ever. If R3's two arrangements are the wrong two, half the reserve is gone for nothing. This is the rival's worst weakness and the draft does not carry it.
- A model written fourth is fitted to R1-R3 and cannot be confirmed by them ("A case a part was fitted on cannot confirm that part"). Its only test is the unspent half plus fresh documents; if either is exhausted first, the model is frozen untested and the file says so.
- Every arm is a new rig: the H61 transport ran one call per report ("The reader is told to read that file and treat it as its whole instruction"), so no arm in either plan has a precedent. If each arm needs its own rig piece, the programme has a list, one item per arrangement, and should say so.
- Two owner's words are spent before any statement of the model exists. If the owner meant the model literally first, the rival has disobeyed the order, and the sketch inside the plan is its only defence.

Known weaknesses of the rival, stated before use.
- Instrument-first delays every answer to Q1-Q5 by one phase.
- Arm (e) may not be available on the service the rig uses; if constrained emission cannot be set, Q1's first clause stays unfalsified in both plans, and the phase plan must say so before it runs.
- The marker-free arm I would most like - L64's own variation test, "change the prose (drop a sentence, deny a clause, swap a name), translate again, and the ledger changes as the commitments do and nowhere else" - trespasses on the Language project's open job ("Not tested: a translator other than Claude") and needs the path fix its README names ("Both drivers point at the machine the rigs were built on"). It stays a candidate, its findings go to RELATIONS as asks, and nothing is written in that project (decision H8).
- R1 judges marking with markers of the same kind, as H69 said of its own judges.

What the rival does not test: anything at the grain of weights or activations; whether any agent understands, is creative or creates knowledge; the skill's own faults; the theory itself; the other model.

PART B - JOB BY JOB: DRAFT AGAINST RIVAL, AND WHAT WOULD SHOW WHICH IS RIGHT

Q1, the harness. DIFFERENT. The draft's answer is M8, and only its second and third clauses get falsifiers (the owner's unsupplied material; arm (d)). By M8's own words arm (d) sets "only what the model reads" and so "replaces nothing" - it cannot bite on the clause that answers Q1. The rival adds arm (e), an emission-port harness, read by a key. What would show which is right: run (e) against the same prompt unconstrained on the keyed half. If hit rates per test are unchanged, the draft loses nothing by omitting it and M8's first clause is wrong or unreached; if they drop while an input-only harness holds, the draft's first test was blind to Q1's own kind of harness.

Q2, stateful against stateless. SAME AT THIS LEVEL on the arms - the rival keeps (a), (b), (c), (d) and P3.1 word for word - and DIFFERENT on the read-out. What would show which is right: R1, which needs no key and no fresh documents. If the struck fields reach 44 of 48 under reworded criteria, the draft's P3.2 stands as written and the instrument phase was idle for this job; if they stay near 38 of 48, the draft's falsifier could never have fired.

Q3, what the context must hold. DIFFERENT. The draft varies how much history a call is handed; the rival removes one of M6's three named items at a time (the frozen question; the parts under test; the change list), which is the skill's Remove test applied to the context itself. What would show which is right: the four-way removal run. If removing the change list moves no certified field, M6's list is too long and the change list is idle in the context - a count the draft's arms cannot produce, because none of them removes one item and keeps the others.

Q4, external memory. DIFFERENT, and the difference is one box. The draft's only run bearing on M7 is in phase 5; the rival's arm (c') puts an agent-written carry-over note in the first run, and reads retrieval provenance off the tool audit the record already keeps. What would show which is right: R2.2. If (c') equals (c), the carrier's author does not matter, M7's declared-against-constructed distinction does no work at the grain of text, and the draft's deferral cost nothing.

Q5, where the attention policy sits. DIFFERENT. The draft's M9 waits on a judge and on phase 5. The rival reads the record's own modules-opened column as the policy's operative use and criticises the policy in the context. What would show which is right: R2.5. The read-out already exists in the record ("Modules opened: idea, by-domain, question-bank, reporting"), so this is a run the repository can make now, and by P1.2's own standard that matters.

Q6, the skill map. DIFFERENT, and here one number decides it. The draft draws the map from "holder today" and predicts at most three holders change; the rival draws it from edit-signature and predicts four or more. Same reading, opposite predictions: P4.1 against R5.1. That is the change that tells the two plans apart for this job, and the draft has already written the count into its own plan.

The end goal, a workflow that embodies the theory. THE SAME AT THIS LEVEL. Both take Part XIV's list of operations as what the workflow must carry; both gate every phase on the owner's word; both refuse to read anything off one report (Derivation 9); both keep the other projects read-only; both end with an answer-keyed run. No change on the change list separates them at the grain of "what the workflow must hold" - only the order in which it is built, and order is not on the list. Following Derivation 2, I report that as the honest result: "A claim that two such candidates 'really' differ is a claim that some admitted change separates them, and must supply it." The finer question that would separate them, recorded as new: is an operation's holder decided by its edit-signature (Part II) or by what does it today? Two queries on one target, so a different question by Part III ("Two questions with the same \(D\) and different \((C,\mathcal Q)\) are different questions").

PART C - THE REPORT

1. The question, frozen. What is explained: why this programme, in this order, with these phases, answers the owner's six unknowns and reaches the end goal. Range: the five phases as written, the record of this repository, and file 10. Asked: does it achieve its purpose - and, for each part, what holds it in place. Kind: purpose-achievement, with production questions inside it (does phase 3 produce evidence about arrangement).

2. The parts and the jobs. Parts: the five phases and their order; M1-M10; the section-6 map sketch; P1.1-P5; the outcome criteria of section 7; what follows either way (8); the programme-failure conditions (9); the weaknesses (10); the exclusions (11); the asks (12); the traps (13). Jobs: Q1-Q6 and the end goal, all GIVEN (H6, quoted); "the map must not be drawn by habit" ADDED (the draft's); "no field carries a claim until two markers agree" ADDED (mine); the two skills frozen and the other projects read-only, FIXED (decisions H6, H7, H8, S4).

3. Part by part (mark, then provenance).
Phase order model-reading-run-map-workflow: held if - held for model-before-map by the added habit job, measured only by P4.1 whose threshold is loose; held for model-before-run by the skill's written-first rule. Provenance built.
Phase 1, the model as first authority: held, by the given job in H6 ("designing a model of LLMs within the language of the semantics needs to be resolved"). Built.
Phase 2, a reading and not a test: held, by a job shown real - two contradictions with evidence in hand (findings 2 and 6). Built.
Phase 3, arms (a)(b)(c): held if - the falsifiers rest on fields struck or uncalibrated. Fitted (to the record's modes-and-repeats shape).
Arm (d): held for M8's third clause; the first clause it cannot reach is left unknown with Poke named. Built.
M1, the declared frame: loose - the draft says "nothing" would count against it, which by the skill's rule makes it a free choice, not an exemption; a near neighbour is "one call plus its tools" in place of "one execution". Asserted.
M2: borrowed - rests on file 10's Part IV and Derivation 3, which section 11 puts outside this test; file 10 itself exposes Derivation 3 under attack (D) and Part XV. Built.
M3: borrowed - Derivation 9, held by its condition "the same input-output projection"; arms with different projections are separable, which is what the plan relies on. Built.
M4: held if - its only holder is fitting evidence (H57 to H59). Fitted.
M5(i): held, by P3.1. M5(ii): held if, on the struck field. The stateful definition: construction, unmarked. Built.
M6: contradicts - the record's OUTSIDE flags and file 54's recall paragraph. Built.
M7: unknown - no arm reaches it; the test that would settle it is the two-retrieval arm over the record, with the tool audit as read-out. Built.
M8 clauses 2 and 3: held if (the owner's material; arm (d)). Clause 1: unknown, with Poke named. Built.
M9: unknown - the modules-opened trace would settle it and no arm uses it. Built.
M10: held - each convention carries a quoted passage, and the one citation I could not check from the results file ("H69's unmapped notion 2") checks out in the rig. Built.
Section 6 map sketch: held if, on P4.1 and P4.2; its rule-application row is loose as written. Fitted.
Section 7 criteria: held for word-list rows; held if for fields, since the criterion H64 said to reword is not reworded.
Sections 9, 10, 11, 12, 13: held - section 9 names the marking as a possible fault, which is the rival's whole case, and section 10 names the writer's and judges' own kind as the exposure.
P3.5's parenthesis: contradicts. The reserve entry: held if.

4. Whole-explanation checks, every Step 5 test by name.
Remove: bit. Phase 2 held (a real contradiction for it to find). Phase 1 has two routes for the job "fix what phase 3 records" - the model, or plan 52's frozen field list plus H64 - so the order's justification survives only for the map and for the written-first rule.
Swap: bit. Arm (c)'s summary-writer swaps to the agent and the prediction changes (finding 14); "five phases" swaps to three with no job lost, so the phase count is loose and what is held is the owner's-word gate per artefact; four thresholds swap freely (finding 12).
Flip the outcome: bit, and the draft passes where it matters - P2.2 covers both outcomes and names the discriminator ("Zero is read one of two ways, decided by P2.1"), which is the good answer, not the loose one. It fails on the phase order: had the plan put the map first, it could have quoted the owner's own "Which skills to have, and where the boundaries lie is the first step" and Derivation 5. So the order is loose relative to the owner's words and held only by the added habit job.
Poke: bit on M2-M7, M9, M10. It cannot bite on M8's first clause, because no change on the list sets an emission port; that clause is left unknown with Poke named.
Reverse: bit on M6 - poke the context and the finding moves; poke the finding and the record shows targets arriving with no context change (the OUTSIDE flags). Direction on the phase order is sound: the plan cites H6's sentence as its cause, and no outcome of a phase moves it.
Hunt the answer in the starting points: bit. The five-phase shape is the planning skill's loop, inherited, and the order is largely H6's own sentence; the only part not already in the starting points is model-before-run-before-map. The conclusion is therefore mostly given rather than derived - which is honest, and the draft says whose it is.
Add a job: bit, and it ruled something out. The added job "the programme must say something about its own judging rounds" finds that H69's five-judge round is already a coarse partition observation sitting in the evidence list (finding 17).
Build the best rival: this return. One change tells the two apart for Q6 (P4.1 against R5.1, opposite predictions on one reading) and one for Q3 (P3.4 against R2.4, where the record is already against the draft). For the end goal, no change on the list tells them apart, and I say so.
Pull: bit. Three pairs. M2 against P3.4 - the line is "any carrier it read", and the record's OUTSIDE flags show it is drawn in the wrong place. P1.2's count against trap 2's ban on counting. "This file fixes the form and the phase plan fixes the number" against Planning file 2's "Every prediction names the count that would falsify it" - the strength of P3.1, P3.2 and P3.3 is set after this file is frozen, and the gauge for that bin is only a trap, not a measurement.
Check the patches: could only half bite. The draft is a first draft - "This is the draft of the research plan" - so it has no rescue history of its own; the test reaches only its inherited held-out lines and its one catch-all (numbers deferred to phase plans, gauged by a trap). Whether this plan narrows its claims quietly under pressure is left unknown with Check the patches named; it cannot be settled until a second numbered file exists.
Look inside: could not bite. The workings are the phase plans, and they do not exist: "Each is a numbered plan of its own when its turn comes, frozen before it runs, on the owner's word", and "the phase plan fixes the number before that phase runs". The parts it would have settled - the arms' rig, the repeat counts, and the denominator of P3.1's "more than two documents" - are left unknown with Look inside named.
What the change list leaves out, stated: the grain of weights (section 1, by choice); the owner's harness material (not in the record); the phase plans' numbers; the skill's own faults; the theory's audit.

5. What would make it harder to vary, in order. (i) Reword the criterion for the same-explanation verdict and re-establish agreement on the 96 reports in hand before phase 3 - it costs no key and no fresh documents, and without it P3.2 and P3.3 cannot fire. (ii) Add one arm that sets an emission port, so that Q1's own kind of harness has a falsifier. (iii) Record which question each run froze, so that P3.3 measures the partition and not the handing-in of the question.

6. What this does not show. Nothing here says the draft is wrong or the rival right. Hard to vary is not true. The draft's model may be right in every part while its phase-3 falsifiers cannot fire; my rival may be better instrumented and still answer the wrong question. Two of the three discriminating counts I name are unrun, and the third (the same-explanation field) is settled only for the criterion as it stands.

7. One next step. Insert the instrument phase before phase 3: rework the three criteria H64 struck, write criteria for the three count-fields the plan invents, add the question-identity field, and re-mark the 96 reports in hand with a blind second marker.
